title: Determination of organic pollutants in Anguilla anguilla by liquid chromatography coupled with tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)
author: Vitale, Picó, et al.
materials: Recovery tests were performed in triplicate for each variation in the water amount. Furthermore, a procedural blank containing non-spiked sample was included at least every 9 samples.

steps.title: Weigh and spike eel tissue
steps.instruction: Place 1 g wet weight of pooled eel liver or muscle into a 50 mL Falcon tube, add 200 µL internal‑standard mix (1 mg mL⁻¹) to reach 20 ng mL⁻¹ in the final extract (assuming 100 % recovery), then add 50 µL external‑standard mix (10 mg mL⁻¹) to give 500 ng g⁻¹, and allow the solvent to evaporate.

steps.title: Add water and acetonitrile
steps.instruction: Add the chosen volume of Milli‑Q water (0, 3, 5, 7.5, or 10 mL – 7.5 mL is used for routine work) to the tube, then add 10 mL acetonitrile (ACN). Vortex the mixture for 3 min to homogenize.

substeps.instruction: Test each water volume (0, 3, 5, 7.5, 10 mL) in separate tubes if method optimisation is required; the 7.5 mL volume was selected as optimal.

steps.title: Add salts and mix
steps.instruction: Add 4 g magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄), 1 g sodium chloride (NaCl), 0.5 g sodium citrate (DCS), and 1 g trisodium citrate dihydrate (TCD) to the tube and shake vigorously by hand for 3 min to prevent salt agglomeration.

steps.title: Centrifuge extraction mixture
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 5 min at 3500 rpm (≈2465 × g).

steps.title: Activate EMR‑Lipid sorbent
steps.instruction: Place the EMR‑Lipid dSPE phase into a clean 15 mL Falcon tube, add 5 mL Milli‑Q water, and vortex for 30 s to activate the sorbent.

steps.title: First cleanup with EMR‑Lipid
steps.instruction: Transfer 5 mL of the QuEChERS supernatant (from the previous centrifugation) into the activated EMR‑Lipid tube, vortex for 30 s, then centrifuge for 5 min at 3500 rpm.

steps.title: Polish extract with MgSO4/NaCl
steps.instruction: Move 5 mL of the EMR‑Lipid supernatant into a new 15 mL Falcon tube containing the polish phase (1600 mg MgSO₄ + 400 mg NaCl), shake manually for 30 s to avoid salt clumping, and centrifuge for 5 min at 3500 rpm.

steps.title: Filter and store extracts
steps.instruction: Filter the final supernatant through a 0.22 µm nylon filter using polypropylene/polyethylene syringes, collect the filtrate in vials with inserts, and store at appropriate temperature until LC‑MS/MS analysis.

steps.title: Prepare LC‑MS/MS system
steps.instruction: Set up an Agilent 1260 UHPLC coupled to an Agilent 6410 triple‑quadrupole MS with electrospray ionisation (ESI) in both positive and negative modes (nebuliser gas 15 psi, gas flow 11 L min⁻¹, ion‑spray voltage 4 kV, source temperature 300 °C). Install two columns: Luna 3 µm C18 (150 × 2 mm) for pesticides/etoricoxib and Kinetex 1.7 µm XB‑C18 (50 × 2.1 mm) for PFAS, illicit drugs and other PPCPs.

substeps.instruction: Positive‑mode mobile phases: A = H₂O + 0.1 % formic acid; B = MeOH + 0.1 % formic acid.
Negative‑mode mobile phases: A = H₂O + 2.5 mM ammonium fluoride; B = MeOH + 2.5 mM ammonium fluoride.
Gradient (both modes): 0 min 70 % A, 12 min 5 % A, 25 min 5 % A, 26 min 70 % A, 30 min 70 % A.
Column temperature 30 °C, injection volume 5 µL, inject ACN extracts directly.

steps.title: Inject samples and run gradient
steps.instruction: Inject each 5 µL sample in MRM mode, using the appropriate column and ionisation polarity (positive for Luna‑column pesticides/etoricoxib, positive for Kinetex‑column PFAS/PPCPs, negative for Kinetex‑column compounds requiring negative mode).

steps.title: Run calibration and quality controls
steps.instruction: Prepare a seven‑point calibration series (5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500 ng mL⁻¹) and inject at the beginning and end of each analytical batch. Include a procedural blank (non‑spiked tissue) at least every nine samples, and inject a 100 ng mL⁻¹ standard every 15 samples to monitor instrumental variation.

steps.title: Perform recovery and validation tests
steps.instruction: For method optimisation, carry out recovery tests in triplicate for each water‑addition level (0, 3, 5, 7.5, 10 mL) and include a procedural blank in each set of nine samples.
